fields.Participants: Procurement Mgr, LP Manager, Legal, Quality
fields.Trigger: Annual vendor program cycle or new vendor onboarding

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "anti-counterfeit requirements into vendor onboarding" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of "updates tier classification annually" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "tracks serialization rate, audit findings, counterfeit incident history" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-444 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Compliance & Anti-Counterfeit Analytics (PA-71.3).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor pushback**: Small vendors lack resources for serialization compliance
- **Competitive pressure**: Stricter requirements may reduce vendor pool
System Touchpoints: - Vendor master with anti-counterfeit tier classification
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 days per onboarding; tier classification ~1 week/year; compliance monitoring ongoing

steps.activity: Procurement incorporates anti-counterfeit requirements into vendor onboarding: product authentication capabilities, serialization standards, packaging security features, supply chain traceability, brand protection cooperation clause; vendors of high-risk categories (power tools, electrical) must demonstrate compliance before activation

LP Manager defines vendor anti-counterfeit tier: Tier 1 (mandatory serialization, quarterly audit) for power tools and premium electrical brands; Tier 2 (serialization recommended, annual audit) for mid-range tools and fixtures; Tier 3 (awareness only) for low-risk categories; updates tier classification annually

Procurement monitors vendor compliance: tracks serialization rate, audit findings, counterfeit incident history; non-compliant vendors receive improvement plan with 90-day deadline; persistent non-compliance affects vendor scorecard and contract renewal

fields.Frequency: Quarterly for Tier 1 vendors; annual for Tier 2
fields.Participants: QA Mgr, LP Manager, Procurement, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Annual audit calendar or incident-triggered audit

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documentation, distribution chain integrity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "records, verification of serialization infrastructure, packaging line…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "QA issues audit report" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-444 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Compliance & Anti-Counterfeit Analytics (PA-71.3).)
- operational: Quality Assurance Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Audit scope limitation**: Remote audits cannot verify physical controls adequately
- **Vendor deception**: Staged factory conditions during audit visits
System Touchpoints: - Audit management system with finding tracking
- Corrective action tracking with deadline alerts

steps.activity: QA Manager prepares audit scope: review vendor manufacturing and packaging controls, serialization processes, raw material traceability, quality testing documentation, distribution chain integrity; for import vendors: include customs documentation verification and origin certification review

QA conducts on-site or remote audit: physical inspection of manufacturing facility, review of quality control records, verification of serialization infrastructure, packaging line observation, sample product testing against BuildRight specifications

QA issues audit report: findings (critical/major/minor), corrective action requests with timeline, re-audit schedule for non-compliant vendors; LP Manager incorporates findings into vendor anti-counterfeit scorecard; Procurement uses findings in contract negotiations

fields.Participants: IT Innovation, LP Manager, CIO, Category Manager
fields.Trigger: Technology refresh cycle or emerging counterfeiting technique

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scanning, invisible ink/taggant marking" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "technologies by ROI and risk severity" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "IT deploys approved technologies" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-444 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Compliance & Anti-Counterfeit Analytics (PA-71.3).)
- operational: IT Innovation Lead review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Technology fragmentation**: Multiple authentication methods create operational complexity
- **Cost vs. benefit**: Advanced technologies (NFC, blockchain) expensive for low-margin categories
System Touchpoints: - Integration architecture for new authentication methods

steps.activity: IT Innovation evaluates anti-counterfeit technologies: NFC tags (vs. QR codes), blockchain-based provenance tracking, AI-powered visual authentication (photo comparison), RFID for bulk scanning, invisible ink/taggant marking; assesses cost, accuracy, scalability, and vendor ecosystem compatibility
LP Manager and Category Manager assess business case: counterfeit loss reduction potential, customer trust improvement, vendor adoption feasibility; prioritizes technologies by ROI and risk severity

IT deploys approved technologies: pilot at 10 stores for 1 category, measure authentication accuracy and operational impact, iterate, then rollout to full network; trains staff on new technology; integrates with existing authentication platform

fields.Participants: LP Analyst, LP Manager, Finance, COO

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "LP Analyst compiles counterfeit financial impact" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews financial impact report" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "counterfeit loss into category P&L" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-444 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Compliance & Anti-Counterfeit Analytics (PA-71.3).)
- operational: LP Analyst review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden costs**: Brand reputation damage and customer trust erosion difficult to quantify
- **Underestimation**: Only detected counterfeits are counted; true loss is higher
System Touchpoints: - LP financial tracking with GL coding
- Executive dashboard with counterfeit loss KPI

steps.activity: LP Analyst compiles counterfeit financial impact: direct losses (counterfeit products sold = margin loss + customer restitution cost), investigation costs (staff time, lab testing, legal fees), prevention costs (serialization infrastructure, training, technology), recovery (vendor credits, insurance claims, legal settlements)

LP Manager reviews financial impact report: total cost of counterfeiting vs. prevention investment budget, cost per incident by category, ROI on anti-counterfeit program; compares against industry benchmarks (retail counterfeit loss typically 1–3% of category sales)

Finance incorporates counterfeit loss into category P&L: adjusts gross margin for affected categories, tracks recovery income, reports to CFO for quarterly executive review; LP Manager proposes budget adjustments based on financial impact trend

fields.Frequency: Annual per key brand; 20–30 key brands
fields.Participants: LP Manager, Category Manager, Vendor Brand Protection Team
fields.Trigger: Annual partnership review or new brand authorization

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "LP Manager establishes brand protection partnership with key vendors" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Vendor provides BuildRight with" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "reports enforcement outcomes to vendor quarterly" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-444 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Compliance & Anti-Counterfeit Analytics (PA-71.3).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor commitment variance**: Some brands actively invest in protection; others are passive
- **Information asymmetry**: Vendors may not share all known counterfeit intelligence

steps.activity: LP Manager establishes brand protection partnership with key vendors: joint investigation protocol, evidence sharing agreement, authentication training and reference material supply, direct communication channel for rapid response to counterfeit incidents

Vendor provides BuildRight with: updated authentic product reference library (images, specifications, security feature guide), counterfeit trend alerts for Philippine market, brand authorization verification API (real-time check if seller is authorized dealer), co-funding for anti-counterfeit technology deployment

LP Manager coordinates joint enforcement: shares intelligence on counterfeit networks, coordinates marketplace takedown actions, participates in vendor-led investigation of supply chain breaches, reports enforcement outcomes to vendor quarterly

fields.Participants: LP Analyst, LP Manager, COO, C-Suite

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scan volume, customer verification requests, vendor compliance rate,…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "counterfeiting technique, major vendor incident, organized ring detection" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "COO includes anti-counterfeit metrics in quarterly executive report" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-444 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Compliance & Anti-Counterfeit Analytics (PA-71.3).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **KPI gaming**: Focusing on detection rate may encourage over-flagging of genuine products
- **Executive attention**: Anti-counterfeit competes with other priorities for executive focus and budget

steps.activity: LP Analyst updates anti-counterfeit KPI dashboard: counterfeit detection rate, authentication scan volume, customer verification requests, vendor compliance rate, investigation resolution time, marketplace takedown success rate, financial impact trend, staff training completion rate

LP Manager presents dashboard to COO: highlights trends, anomalies, and action items; escalates critical issues (new counterfeiting technique, major vendor incident, organized ring detection); recommends resource allocation adjustments

COO includes anti-counterfeit metrics in quarterly executive report: program ROI, risk assessment by category, strategic initiatives progress; presented to CEO and Board as part of risk management update

Pain Points / Risks: - **Competitive sensitivity**: Reluctance to share detailed intelligence with competitors

steps.activity: LP Manager participates in industry anti-counterfeit forums: Philippine Retailers Association LP committee, IPOPHL (Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines) consultations, DTI consumer protection coordination; shares anonymized intelligence on counterfeiting trends and methods

LP Manager exchanges intelligence with peer retailers (anonymized, non-competitive): counterfeit source identification, common modus operandi, vendor integrity concerns, marketplace enforcement challenges; receives intelligence in return that improves BuildRight's detection capability

LP Manager contributes to policy advocacy: supports stronger IP enforcement through industry associations, provides retail-sector perspective to IPOPHL and DTI on counterfeiting impact, participates in draft regulation consultations affecting product authentication requirements

fields.Participants: COO, LP Manager, Category Mgr, CIO, CFO, VP Legal

workflows.name: Annual Anti-Counterfeit Strategy Review & Program Update

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "technology ROI evaluation, vendor compliance trend, financial impact analysis,…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review with all stakeholders" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "LP Manager develops annual action plan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-444 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Compliance & Anti-Counterfeit Analytics (PA-71.3).)
- operational: COO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Budget pressure**: Anti-counterfeit program competes with revenue-generating investments
- **Threat evolution**: Annual review cadence may be too slow for rapidly evolving counterfeiting techniques

steps.activity: LP Manager prepares annual anti-counterfeit program review: year-over-year metrics comparison, program effectiveness assessment, technology ROI evaluation, vendor compliance trend, financial impact analysis, emerging threat assessment

Cross-functional strategy session: COO leads review with all stakeholders; assesses program performance vs. objectives; identifies gaps and emerging risks; sets next-year targets: counterfeit detection rate, vendor compliance rate, financial loss reduction, technology deployment milestones

LP Manager develops annual action plan: budget request for technology investments, vendor engagement priorities, training calendar, enforcement focus areas, staffing needs; CFO approves budget; COO signs off on strategy
